Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202202187. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Add 16.2 g of the powder of this medicine per 1 litre of lukewarm water and prepare the solution by stirring intermittently for at least 15 minutes until it is completely dissolved. Use this medicine in the following order. Wash the instruments to be sterilised first, then immerse them completely in this activated solution and leave them soaking for 10 minutes. Keep the container of this solution closed during use. After the recommended contact time has elapsed, rinse the medical devices with water of at least drinking-water quality and dry them. The solution must be prepared daily and must be replaced immediately if it becomes contaminated.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use it on the human body.
  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If pain continues, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for 15 minutes and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Delayed or insufficient rinsing may cause damage to the eyes.
  • If the vapour is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for hyperhidrosis, in which excessive sweating occurs in the armpits, hands and feet.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202301701. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the application area in the evening and wash it off with water the next morning. Use it once every night until perspiration, that is sweating, stops, and once the symptoms improve reduce it to 1 to 2 uses a week.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to it.
  • Do not use it on skin shaved within the previous 12 hours or on damaged or irritated skin.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women, breastfeeding women and children (aged 12 years or younger) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it only on the area to be treated.
  • Avoid contact with the eyes, nostrils, mouth or other mucous membranes.
  • If accidental contact occurs, wash it off thoroughly with water.
  • When a breastfeeding woman uses it, be careful that this medicine does not touch the breast area.
  • If it does, wash off every trace of the medicine thoroughly, however small, before starting to breastfeed.
  • To avoid a burning sensation of the skin, dry the treatment area completely before using this medicine.
  • Avoid direct contact with clothing, jewellery and polished metal surfaces.

Possible side effects

  • After using this medicine, the reduction in sweating may temporarily cause a feeling of irritation or redness with congestion of the skin.
  • If these symptoms become severe, suspend use of this medicine.
  • If irritation or hypersensitivity reactions including dermatitis occur at the application site, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If application site reactions such as pain, itching, erythema, rash or a burning sensation of the skin occur rarely, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use depilatories on the affected area within 12 hours before or after using this medicine.

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfection during surgery, personal hand disinfection, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site before surgery.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfect

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200201841. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For cleansing of general skin and wounded areas, wet the area to be cleansed with water, use only the minimum amount needed for application to the skin or wound, apply it and then wipe it off gently. Rinse thoroughly with water. For hand disinfection during surgery, wet the hands and forearms with water, apply 5 mL of this product to the hands and up to the elbows and rub for about 3 minutes using a brush or a sponge. Rinse thoroughly under running water, repeat the above procedure once more and then dry completely. For personal hand disinfection, wet the hands with water, apply 5 mL of this product to the hands and rub both hands vigorously for 15 seconds. Rinse with water and dry completely. For disinfection of the skin before surgery, apply a sufficient amount to the surgical site and rub for at least 2 minutes. Dry with a sterile towel, repeat the above procedure once more and then dry with a sterile towel.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to other medicines, a patient with an allergic disease such as asthma or a history or family history of one, a woman who is pregnant or may be pregnant, or a breastfeeding woman.
  • Use this medicine externally only; do not take it orally and do not inject it.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause serious corneal damage that can require a corneal transplant (corneal erosion, epithelial defect / corneal damage, severe permanent visual impairment), so take care to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get in, rinse them thoroughly with clean water immediately.
  • This medicine is adsorbed onto textiles and cloth (cotton, gauze, wool, rayon and the like), so when it is used by soaking such material, supply fresh solution whenever the effective concentration is no longer maintained.
  • Anions contained in saline and similar solutions form poorly soluble salts, so use clean distilled water when diluting it.
  • Replace the diluted solution used for washing the hands and similar purposes with fresh solution at least once a day.

Possible side effects

  • If shock occurs rarely (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, redness), if hypersensitivity such as rash or hives occurs occasionally, or if fatal anaphylactic shock of unknown frequency occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Photosensitisation may occur.

Interactions

  • Organic substances such as serum and pus, and soaps, weaken the disinfectant action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.

This medicine is used for the sterilisation and disinfection of medical instruments.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilisation and disinfection of medical instruments.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202105124. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. First, immerse the pre-cleaned medical instruments completely in the disinfectant solution. For instruments and machinery with fine pores or a complex structure, use pressure injection or suction so that they are thoroughly wetted with the prepared disinfectant solution. Perform a leak test first if necessary. Immerse completely for at least 5 minutes, or for at least 6 minutes in the case of tubercle bacilli. After thorough immersion, remove the items and rinse them with at least 200 mL of running sterile purified water, or with water according to the purpose of use. For instruments with fine pores or a complex structure the disinfectant solution tends to remain inside, so rinse thoroughly by pressure-injecting sterile purified water or water, or by extending the rinsing time.

Warning

  • Do not use it on the human body.

Precautions for use

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and then consult a doctor.
  • If the vapour is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and then consult a doctor.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and consult a doctor.
  • Clean thoroughly before disinfection to remove visible contaminants.
  • Take sufficient care in storage and handling so that it is not drunk or swallowed by mistake.
  • When disposing of the disinfectant solution, flush it away with a large amount of water.

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201708524. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Mix 4 L of agent 1 with 90 mL of agent 2. Use this medicine in the following order. First, immerse the pre-cleaned medical instruments completely in the prepared disinfectant solution. For instruments and machinery with fine pores or a complex structure, use pressure injection or suction so that they are thoroughly wetted with the prepared disinfectant solution. Depending on the purpose of use, a large volume of water may be used; for instruments with fine pores or a complex structure the disinfectant solution tends to remain inside, so rinse thoroughly by pressure-injecting sterile purified water or water, or by extending the rinsing time. After disinfection of the medical instruments is complete and before the instruments are used, always check for residues of this medicine using a hydrogen peroxide residue test strip or similar and confirm that the level is below 0.5 ppm as hydrogen peroxide.

  • Do not use it on the human body.

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If pain continues, obtain treatment from a dermatologist.

For disinfection of the hands and skin (excluding hand disinfection of health and hygiene workers and of the operator during surgery, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site) use a 0.1 to 0.5% aqueous solution; for disinfection of medical devices use a 0.1 to 0.5% aqueous solution; for disinfection of furniture and instruments and for disinfection of wounded areas of the skin use a 0.05% aqueous solution.

  • Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it, and do not use it on the brain, spinal cord, ear (inner, middle or outer ear), vagina, bladder, oral cavity or other mucosal surfaces, or on the eyes.
  • Patients with hypersensitivity to other medicines and patients with an allergic disease such as asthma or a history or family history of one should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only; do not take it orally and do not inject it.
  • When it is used over a wide area or for a long period, take care not to inhale the vapour.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so take care to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get in, rinse them thoroughly with clean water immediately.
  • Do not use it for obstetric and gynaecological purposes (such as disinfection of the vagina and vulva) or for urological purposes (such as disinfection of the external genitalia and mucosal surfaces).
  • When disinfecting instruments that may come into contact with nerves or mucosal surfaces, such as syringes and catheters, rinse them thoroughly with sterile water before use.
  • Replace the diluted solution used for washing the hands and similar purposes with fresh solution at least once a day.

Possible side effects

  • If shock occurs rarely (for example nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, redness), or if hypersensitivity symptoms such as rash or hives occur occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Photosensitisation may occur.

Interactions

  • Organic substances such as serum and pus, and soaps, weaken the disinfectant action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.

Rinse the instruments completely with sterile water so that no solution remains. Use them after drying, or store them by an appropriate method.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine on the human body.
  • When using and storing the activated solution, use a container with a lid or similar to prevent the vapour from spreading, and at the same time take care to ventilate the area.
  • Handle it with sufficient care, for example by wearing protective equipment such as goggles, gloves and a mask, to protect the eyes and skin and to avoid inhaling the powder of this medicine.
  • Clean thoroughly before disinfection to remove visible contaminants.
  • Take sufficient care in storage and handling so that it is not drunk or swallowed by mistake.

Possible side effects

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If pain continues, obtain treatment from a dermatologist.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and obtain examination by an ophthalmologist.
  • Delayed or insufficient rinsing may cause damage to the eyes.
  • If the vapour is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and consult a specialist.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and obtain examination by a specialist.
  • Forced vomiting may cause damage to the respiratory system.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve inflammation caused by dentures, oral candidiasis such as thrush, gingivitis, pharyngit

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201700798. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use it in the mouth

Rinse the mouth with 15 mL per dose for about 1 minute, 2 times a day; in the case of stomatitis caused by dentures, soak and clean the dentures for 15 minutes 2 times a day. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Warning

  • Do not use it for a long period, because it may cause an imbalance of the normal bacterial flora in the mouth.

Precautions for use

  • People who have experienced hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Patients who have an allergic disease such as asthma or who have such a history or a family history, pregnant women, breast-feeding women and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it only for gargling and do not use it internally.

  • Temporary parotitis, an increase in staining on the teeth or the surface of the mouth (the inside of the mouth), an increase in the formation of supragingival calculus, a change in the sense of taste and the like may occur.
  • If, rarely, symptoms of shock (for example, nausea, discomfort, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty in breathing, seizure) or, occasionally, rash or urticaria occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201701117. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use it as the undiluted solution. Use this medicine in the following order. Immerse the medical instruments completely in the disinfectant solution for about 1 minute (within 5 minutes). For instruments with fine pores, such as endoscopes, be careful to ensure sufficient contact. After thorough immersion, remove the items and rinse them under running sterile purified water for at least 15 seconds, or with water according to the purpose of use. For instruments with fine pores or a complex structure the disinfectant solution tends to remain inside, so rinse thoroughly by pressure-injecting sterile purified water or water, or by extending the rinsing time.

Warning

  • Do not use it on the human body.

Precautions for use

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and then consult a doctor.
  • If the vapour is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and then consult a doctor.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and consult a doctor.
  • During use and storage, use a container with a lid or similar to prevent the vapour from spreading, and at the same time take care to ventilate the area.
  • Handle it with sufficient care, for example by wearing protective equipment such as goggles, so that it never gets into the eyes.
  • Wash contaminated reusable devices thoroughly before disinfection.
  • When disinfecting devices, wear gloves of an appropriate type and length, eye protection and a waterproof gown.
  • Users must follow the instructions for use.
  • Use a test strip to measure the concentration before use.
  • After washing, remove the moisture thoroughly and then immerse the items in the prepared disinfectant solution.
  • Repeated use may cause degradation of natural rubber and raw rubber, such as cracking.
  • Do not use it on cracked or rusted instruments.
  • During washing and disinfection, wear protective equipment such as rubber gloves, a gown, a mask and protective goggles to prevent contact with or inhalation of infectious material and of the disinfectant solution.
  • Take sufficient care in storage and handling so that it is not drunk or swallowed by mistake.

Who should ask first

How to apply it

For disinfection of the hands and skin, wash for about 5 minutes with a 0.05 to 0.2 % aqueous solution and then wipe clean with sterile gauze or cloth. For disinfection of the skin at the surgical site, wash the skin surface to be operated on with a 0.1 % aqueous solution for about 5 minutes and then apply a 0.2 % aqueous solution. For disinfection of the mucous membranes at the surgical site and for disinfection of wounded areas of the skin and mucous membranes, use a 0.01 to 0.05 % aqueous solution. For disinfection of medical devices, immerse them in a 0.05 to 0.2 % aqueous solution for 10 to 15 minutes; however, for disinfection related to tuberculosis patients use a 0.2 to 0.5 % aqueous solution. For disinfection of operating room and ward furniture, instruments and articles, use a 0.05 to 0.2 % aqueous solution; however, for disinfection related to tuberculosis patients use a 0.2 to 0.5 % aqueous solution.

  • Do not mix this medicine with other disinfectants.

  • Soaps weaken the bactericidal action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the chemical sterilisation and bactericidal disinfection of medical instruments.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201701117. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use it as the undiluted solution. Use this medicine in the following order. Immerse the medical instruments completely in the disinfectant solution for about 1 minute (within 5 minutes). For instruments with fine pores, such as endoscopes, be careful to ensure sufficient contact. After thorough immersion, remove the items and rinse them under running sterile purified water for at least 15 seconds, or with water according to the purpose of use. For instruments with fine pores or a complex structure the disinfectant solution tends to remain inside, so rinse thoroughly by pressure-injecting sterile purified water or water, or by extending the rinsing time.

Warning

  • Do not use it on the human body.

Precautions for use

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and then consult a doctor.
  • If the vapour is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and then consult a doctor.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and consult a doctor.
  • During use and storage, use a container with a lid or similar to prevent the vapour from spreading, and at the same time take care to ventilate the area.
  • Handle it with sufficient care, for example by wearing protective equipment such as goggles, so that it never gets into the eyes.
  • Wash contaminated reusable devices thoroughly before disinfection.
  • When disinfecting devices, wear gloves of an appropriate type and length, eye protection and a waterproof gown.
  • Users must follow the instructions for use.
  • Use a test strip to measure the concentration before use.
  • After washing, remove the moisture thoroughly and then immerse the items in the prepared disinfectant solution.
  • Repeated use may cause degradation of natural rubber and raw rubber, such as cracking.
  • Do not use it on cracked or rusted instruments.
  • During washing and disinfection, wear protective equipment such as rubber gloves, a gown, a mask and protective goggles to prevent contact with or inhalation of infectious material and of the disinfectant solution.
  • Take sufficient care in storage and handling so that it is not drunk or swallowed by mistake.

At a glance

Category

How it works

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use it in the mouth

Rinse the mouth with 15 mL per dose for about 1 minute, 2 times a day; in the case of stomatitis caused by dentures, soak and clean the dentures for 15 minutes 2 times a day. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Warning

  • Do not use it for a long period, because it may cause an imbalance of the normal bacterial flora in the mouth.

Precautions for use

  • People who have experienced hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.

payloads.summary: This medicine is used for the bactericidal disinfection of corrugated tubing, silicone tubes, vinyl tubes, silicone caps
payloads.content:

Topical medicine (MFDS 201708524)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201708524. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the bactericidal disinfection of corrugated tubing, silicone tubes, vinyl tubes, silicone caps, silicone stoppers, scalpel handles and endoscopes.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the bactericidal disinfection of corrugated tubing, silicone tubes, vinyl tubes, silicone caps

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201708524. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Mix 4 L of agent 1 with 90 mL of agent 2. Use this medicine in the following order. First, immerse the pre-cleaned medical instruments completely in the prepared disinfectant solution. For instruments and machinery with fine pores or a complex structure, use pressure injection or suction so that they are thoroughly wetted with the prepared disinfectant solution. Perform a leak test first if necessary. Immerse completely for at least 5 minutes. If sporicidal action is required, immerse completely for at least 10 minutes. After thorough immersion, remove the items and rinse them under running sterile purified water for at least 15 seconds. Depending on the purpose of use, a large volume of water may be used; for instruments with fine pores or a complex structure the disinfectant solution tends to remain inside, so rinse thoroughly by pressure-injecting sterile purified water or water, or by extending the rinsing time. After disinfection of the medical instruments is complete and before the instruments are used, always check for residues of this medicine using a hydrogen peroxide residue test strip or similar and confirm that the level is below 0.5 ppm as hydrogen peroxide.

Warning

  • Do not use it on the human body.

Precautions for use

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If pain continues, obtain treatment from a dermatologist.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and obtain examination by an ophthalmologist.
  • Delayed or insufficient rinsing may cause damage to the eyes.
  • If the vapour is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and consult a specialist.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and obtain examination by a specialist.
  • Forced vomiting may cause damage to the respiratory system.
  • Handle it with sufficient care, for example by wearing protective equipment such as goggles, so that it never gets into the eyes.
  • If it does get into the eyes, wash them with a large amount of water and then obtain treatment from a specialist.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with chlorine-based preparations such as hypochlorites.

How it works

Why this one

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply the sponge soaked with the solution of this medicine to the hands and up to the elbows and rub by hand for 3 minutes. Rub the nails, the cuticles and the areas between the fingers with particular care. Use a brush to rub if necessary. Rinse with warm water, repeat the procedure washing for 3 minutes, rinse thoroughly with water and dry completely.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it, and do not use it on the brain, spinal cord, ear, vagina, bladder, oral cavity or other mucosal surfaces, on the eyes, or on eroded (macerated) or suppurating areas.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to other medicines, with an allergic disease such as asthma or a history or family history of one, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are breastfeeding.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration exactly.
  • Use this medicine externally only; do not take it orally and do not inject it.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so take care to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get in, rinse them thoroughly with clean water immediately.
  • This medicine is adsorbed onto textiles and cloth (cotton, gauze, wool, rayon and the like), so when it is used by soaking such material, supply fresh solution whenever the effective concentration is no longer maintained.
  • Replace the diluted solution used for washing the hands with fresh solution at least once a day.

  • If shock occurs rarely (nausea, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, redness and the like), or if rash or hives occurs occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Organic substances such as serum and pus, and soaps, weaken the disinfectant action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for hand disinfection during surgery and for hygienic purposes.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200707111. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine undiluted, as the neat solution. When it is used for hand disinfection by the operator during surgery, dispense 5 mL of this medicine into the palm, spread it evenly over both hands and arms (up to the elbows), then rub for at least 3 minutes while allowing it to dry, and carry this out 2 times. When it is used for hand disinfection for hygienic purposes, dispense 3 mL of this medicine into the palm, spread it evenly over both hands, then rub for 30 seconds while allowing it to dry.

Warning

  • This medicine is flammable, so keep it away from ignition sources such as lit cigarettes.
  • Use it externally only; it must not be used internally.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine on areas with insufficient blood supply, on wounded areas, on the eyes, on mucous membranes or on ulcerated areas.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration exactly.
  • When using it on a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Use it topically on the skin only.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with water.

Possible side effects

This medicine is used for disinfection of the hands and skin, disinfection of the skin at the surgical site, disinfection of the mucous membranes at the surgical site, disinfection of wounded areas of the skin and mucous membranes, disinfection of medical devices, and disinfection of operating room and ward furniture, instruments and articles.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the hands and skin, disinfection of the skin at the surgical site, disinfectio

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201602963. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For disinfection of the hands and skin, wash for about 5 minutes with a 0.05 to 0.2 % aqueous solution and then wipe clean with sterile gauze or cloth. For disinfection of the skin at the surgical site, wash the skin surface to be operated on with a 0.1 % aqueous solution for about 5 minutes and then apply a 0.2 % aqueous solution. For disinfection of the mucous membranes at the surgical site and for disinfection of wounded areas of the skin and mucous membranes, use a 0.01 to 0.05 % aqueous solution. For disinfection of medical devices, immerse them in a 0.05 to 0.2 % aqueous solution for 10 to 15 minutes; however, for disinfection related to tuberculosis patients use a 0.2 to 0.5 % aqueous solution. For disinfection of operating room and ward furniture, instruments and articles, use a 0.05 to 0.2 % aqueous solution; however, for disinfection related to tuberculosis patients use a 0.2 to 0.5 % aqueous solution.

Precautions for use

  • Do not mix this medicine with other disinfectants.
  • Use it externally only.
  • Soaps weaken the bactericidal action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Be careful to keep the undiluted or concentrated solution out of the eyes, and if it does get in, rinse the eyes thoroughly with water.
  • When a concentrated solution is used, irritation of the skin and mucous membranes may occur, so use it with care.
  • If iron instruments have to be immersed for a long time, dissolve sodium nitrite in the solution to prevent corrosion, except for copper items.
  • (This does not affect the bactericidal action.)

Possible side effects

  • If rash or itching occurs occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Rinse the mouth with 15 mL per dose for about 1 minute, 2 times a day; in the case of stomatitis caused by dentures, soak and clean the dentures for 15 minutes 2 times a day. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Category

How it works

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfect

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199806429. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, wet the area to be cleansed with water, use only the minimum amount needed for application to the skin or wound, apply it and then wipe it off gently. Then rinse thoroughly with water. For personal hand disinfection, wet the hands with water, apply 5 mL of this product to the hands and rub both hands vigorously for 15 seconds. Then rinse with water and dry completely.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women must not use this medicine.

  • This medicine is adsorbed onto textiles and cloth (cotton, gauze, wool, rayon and the like), so when it is used by soaking such material, supply fresh solution whenever the effective concentration is no longer maintained.
  • Anions contained in saline and similar solutions form poorly soluble salts, so use clean distilled water when diluting it.
  • Replace the diluted solution used for washing the hands and similar purposes with fresh solution at least once a day.

  • Use it topically on the skin only.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with water.

Possible side effects

  • Contact dermatitis and photosensitivity may occur, and rarely itching, redness or dryness of the skin.

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfection during surgery, personal hand disinfection, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site before surgery.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfect

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199806429. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, wet the area to be cleansed with water, use only the minimum amount needed for application to the skin or wound, apply it and then wipe it off gently. Then rinse thoroughly with water. For personal hand disinfection, wet the hands with water, apply 5 mL of this product to the hands and rub both hands vigorously for 15 seconds. Then rinse with water and dry completely.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity to other medicines and anyone who has experienced an allergic disease such as asthma should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine externally only; do not take it orally and do not inject it.
  • Do not use it on the eyes, ears or mouth, or on extensive wounds or burns.
  • Soaps weaken the bactericidal action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • This medicine is adsorbed onto textiles and cloth (cotton, gauze, wool, rayon and the like), so when it is used by soaking such material, supply fresh solution whenever the effective concentration is no longer maintained.
  • Anions contained in saline and similar solutions form poorly soluble salts, so use clean distilled water when diluting it.
  • Replace the diluted solution used for washing the hands and similar purposes with fresh solution at least once a day.

Possible side effects

  • If shock, nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing or redness occurs rarely, or if rash or hives occurs occasionally, or if anaphylactic shock of unknown frequency occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Photosensitisation may occur.

This medicine is used for hand disinfection during surgery and for hygienic purposes.

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200707111. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine undiluted, as the neat solution. When it is used for hand disinfection by the operator during surgery, dispense 5 mL of this medicine into the palm, spread it evenly over both hands and arms (up to the elbows), then rub for at least 3 minutes while allowing it to dry, and carry this out 2 times. When it is used for hand disinfection for hygienic purposes, dispense 3 mL of this medicine into the palm, spread it evenly over both hands, then rub for 30 seconds while allowing it to dry.

  • This medicine is flammable, so keep it away from ignition sources such as lit cigarettes.
  • Use it externally only; it must not be used internally.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine on areas with insufficient blood supply, on wounded areas, on the eyes, on mucous membranes or on ulcerated areas.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration exactly.
  • When using it on a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Use it topically on the skin only.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with water.

Possible side effects

  • Contact dermatitis and photosensitivity may occur, and rarely itching, redness or dryness of the skin.

Topical medicine (MFDS 201902449)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201902449. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for cleansing of general skin and of wounded areas no deeper than the surface layer of the skin, for personal hand disinfection, and for disinfection of the skin at the surgical site before surgery.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for cleansing of general skin and of wounded areas no deeper than t

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201902449. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For cleansing of general skin and of wounded areas no deeper than the surface layer of the skin, wet the area to be cleansed with water, apply the minimum needed for application to the skin or wound and wipe it off gently. Rinse thoroughly with water. Discard after a single use. For personal hand disinfection, wet the hands with water and rub vigorously for 15 seconds with 1 sheet of this product. Rinse with water and dry completely. Discard after a single use. For disinfection of the skin before surgery, use a sufficient number of sheets and rub the surgical site for at least 2 minutes. Dry with a sterile towel, repeat the above procedure once more and then dry with a sterile towel. Discard after a single use.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, anyone who has experienced allergic symptoms (such as asthma) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine externally only.
  • Do not use it on the head, the face, areas in contact with the meninges, the genital area, wounds deeper than the surface layer of the skin, the eyes, the ears, the mouth, extensive wounds or burns.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Soaps weaken the bactericidal action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.

Possible side effects

  • If shock, nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing or redness (congested and reddened skin) occurs rarely, or if hypersensitivity symptoms such as rash or hives occur occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Photosensitisation may occur.

This medicine is used to relieve inflammation caused by prostheses (dentures), oral candidiasis such as thrush, gingivitis, pharyngitis and aphthous stomatitis, and for bactericidal disinfection after periodontal ligament surgery.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oromucosal medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve inflammation caused by prostheses (dentures), oral candidiasis such as thrush, gingivit

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202003209. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use it in the mouth

Rinse the mouth with 15 mL per dose for about 1 minute, 2 times a day; in the case of stomatitis caused by dentures, soak and clean the dentures for 15 minutes 2 times a day. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to it.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with an allergic disease such as asthma or anyone who has experienced one, pregnant women, breastfeeding women, children under 18 years of age, and anyone who has experienced hypersensitivity or an allergy to propylene glycol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It may cause an imbalance of the normal bacterial flora in the oral cavity, so do not normally use it for more than 10 days.
  • Use it as a mouthwash only and do not use it internally.
  • It may cause staining of oral surfaces such as the tooth surfaces, prostheses and the underside of the tongue.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms occur rarely (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, seizures), or if rash or hives occurs occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Temporary parotitis, increased staining of the teeth and of the surfaces of the oral cavity (inside of the mouth), increased formation of supragingival calculus, changes in taste sensation, desquamation of the oral (inside of the mouth) mucosa in children, and mild irritation may occur.

This medicine is used for hand disinfection during surgery and for hygienic purposes.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for hand disinfection during surgery and for hygienic purposes.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200707111. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine undiluted, as the neat solution. When it is used for hand disinfection by the operator during surgery, dispense 5 mL of this medicine into the palm, spread it evenly over both hands and arms (up to the elbows), then rub for at least 3 minutes while allowing it to dry, and carry this out 2 times. When it is used for hand disinfection for hygienic purposes, dispense 3 mL of this medicine into the palm, spread it evenly over both hands, then rub for 30 seconds while allowing it to dry.

Warning

  • This medicine is flammable, so keep it away from ignition sources such as lit cigarettes.
  • Use it externally only; it must not be used internally.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine on areas with insufficient blood supply, on wounded areas, on the eyes, on mucous membranes or on ulcerated areas.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration exactly.
  • When using it on a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Use it topically on the skin only.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with water.

Possible side effects

  • Contact dermatitis and photosensitivity may occur, and rarely itching, redness or dryness of the skin.

Oromucosal medicine (MFDS 201700798)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201700798. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to relieve inflammation caused by dentures, oral candidiasis such as thrush, gingivitis, pharyngitis and aphthous stomatitis, and for sterilization and disinfection after periodontal membrane surgery.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oromucosal medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve inflammation caused by dentures, oral candidiasis such as thrush, gingivitis, pharyngit

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201700798. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use it in the mouth

Rinse the mouth with 15 mL per dose for about 1 minute, 2 times a day; in the case of stomatitis caused by dentures, soak and clean the dentures for 15 minutes 2 times a day. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Warning

  • Do not use it for a long period, because it may cause an imbalance of the normal bacterial flora in the mouth.

Precautions for use

  • People who have experienced hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Patients who have an allergic disease such as asthma or who have such a history or a family history, pregnant women, breast-feeding women and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it only for gargling and do not use it internally.

Possible side effects

  • Temporary parotitis, an increase in staining on the teeth or the surface of the mouth (the inside of the mouth), an increase in the formation of supragingival calculus, a change in the sense of taste and the like may occur.
  • If, rarely, symptoms of shock (for example, nausea, discomfort, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty in breathing, seizure) or, occasionally, rash or urticaria occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This leaflet supports in-store consultation. Ask a pharmacist at the store about product choice and use. Products with the same ingredient, strength and form are managed to the same quality standard. Check by ingredient and strength rather than by product name.

Topical medicine (MFDS 199806429)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199806429. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfection during surgery, personal hand disinfection, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site before surgery.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfect

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199806429. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, wet the area to be cleansed with water, use only the minimum amount needed for application to the skin or wound, apply it and then wipe it off gently. Then rinse thoroughly with water. For personal hand disinfection, wet the hands with water, apply 5 mL of this product to the hands and rub both hands vigorously for 15 seconds. Then rinse with water and dry completely.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity to other medicines and anyone who has experienced an allergic disease such as asthma should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine externally only; do not take it orally and do not inject it.
  • Do not use it on the eyes, ears or mouth, or on extensive wounds or burns.
  • Soaps weaken the bactericidal action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • This medicine is adsorbed onto textiles and cloth (cotton, gauze, wool, rayon and the like), so when it is used by soaking such material, supply fresh solution whenever the effective concentration is no longer maintained.
  • Anions contained in saline and similar solutions form poorly soluble salts, so use clean distilled water when diluting it.
  • Replace the diluted solution used for washing the hands and similar purposes with fresh solution at least once a day.

Possible side effects

  • If shock, nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing or redness occurs rarely, or if rash or hives occurs occasionally, or if anaphylactic shock of unknown frequency occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Photosensitisation may occur.

This medicine is used to relieve gingivitis, stomatitis, thrush, conditions before and after tooth extraction, pharyngitis, tonsillitis, and oral mucositis caused by physical factors such as radiotherapy and intubation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oromucosal medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve gingivitis, stomatitis, thrush, conditions before and after tooth extraction, pharyngit

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202104954. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use it in the mouth

Rinse the mouth with 1 sachet (15 mL) per dose, 2 to 3 times a day, using it undiluted or diluted with a small amount of water. Do not use it continuously for 7 days or more without the guidance and supervision of a doctor. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Precautions for use

  • Do not administer this medicine to patients with hypersensitivity to it or to children aged 12 years or younger.
  • After rinsing the mouth, spit it out and do not swallow it.

Possible side effects

  • Belching, nausea and vomiting may occur, occasionally a feeling of numbness in the mouth, a pricking sensation or a burning sensation, and rarely hypersensitivity reactions.

Interactions

  • If you use antipyretic analgesics, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

payloads.title: Topical medicine (MFDS 201701117)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used for the chemical sterilisation and bactericidal disinfection of medical instruments.
payloads.content:
Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicineThis medicine is used for the chemical sterilisation and bactericidal disinfection of medical instruments.

Topical medicine (MFDS 201701117)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201701117. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the chemical sterilisation and bactericidal disinfection of medical instruments.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the chemical sterilisation and bactericidal disinfection of medical instruments.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201701117. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use it as the undiluted solution. Use this medicine in the following order. Immerse the medical instruments completely in the disinfectant solution for about 1 minute (within 5 minutes). For instruments with fine pores, such as endoscopes, be careful to ensure sufficient contact. After thorough immersion, remove the items and rinse them under running sterile purified water for at least 15 seconds, or with water according to the purpose of use. For instruments with fine pores or a complex structure the disinfectant solution tends to remain inside, so rinse thoroughly by pressure-injecting sterile purified water or water, or by extending the rinsing time.

Warning

  • Do not use it on the human body.

Precautions for use

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and then consult a doctor.
  • If the vapour is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and then consult a doctor.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and consult a doctor.
  • During use and storage, use a container with a lid or similar to prevent the vapour from spreading, and at the same time take care to ventilate the area.
  • Handle it with sufficient care, for example by wearing protective equipment such as goggles, so that it never gets into the eyes.
  • Wash contaminated reusable devices thoroughly before disinfection.
  • When disinfecting devices, wear gloves of an appropriate type and length, eye protection and a waterproof gown.
  • Users must follow the instructions for use.
  • Use a test strip to measure the concentration before use.
  • After washing, remove the moisture thoroughly and then immerse the items in the prepared disinfectant solution.
  • Repeated use may cause degradation of natural rubber and raw rubber, such as cracking.

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201403893. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Spray from a distance of 15 to 26 cm from the area to be treated, several times a day every 3 to 4 hours. Spraying forms a thin powdery film, which may be covered with a bandage if necessary. Shake well before use.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to it, in children aged 2 years or younger, or in patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goitre, endemic goitre, Hashimoto's thyroiditis and the like), renal failure or dermatitis herpetiformis, or in patients undergoing radioactive iodine therapy or in the period before and after such therapy.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a seriously ill patient (such as a burn patient), if you have thyroid disease or a history of renal failure, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
  • Do not use it ophthalmically or internally.
  • Take care to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations.

  • If shock symptoms occur rarely (difficulty breathing, flushing, hives and the like), or iodine rash, or occasionally pain, itching, irritation, rash, congested and reddened skin or dermatitis, or rarely a burning sensation, skin ulcers or skin discolouration, or rarely small blisters, or very rarely angioedema, or symptoms of thyroid abnormality including tension, depressed mood, difficulty sleeping, trembling of the hands, a fast or irregular heartbeat, abnormal breathing, a feeling of heat or sweating, weight loss, weight gain and fatigue, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve inflammation caused by prostheses (dentures), oral candidiasis such as thrush, gingivit

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202003209. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use it in the mouth

Rinse the mouth with 15 mL per dose for about 1 minute, 2 times a day; in the case of stomatitis caused by dentures, soak and clean the dentures for 15 minutes 2 times a day. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine in patients with hypersensitivity to it.

  • If shock symptoms occur rarely (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, seizures), or if rash or hives occurs occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Temporary parotitis, increased staining of the teeth and of the surfaces of the oral cavity (inside of the mouth), increased formation of supragingival calculus, changes in taste sensation, desquamation of the oral (inside of the mouth) mucosa in children, and mild irritation may occur.

Apply it to the area to be disinfected.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the bactericidal disinfection of the operator's hands and arms.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200901684. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply the sponge soaked with the solution to the hands and up to the elbows and rub by hand for 5 minutes. Use a brush if necessary, rubbing the nails, the cuticles and the areas between the fingers with particular care. Then rinse with warm water, repeat the procedure washing for 3 minutes, rinse thoroughly with water and dry slowly.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to iodine, patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goitre, endemic goitre, Hashimoto's thyroiditis and the like), dermatitis herpetiformis, renal failure or serious illness (such as burn patients), women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women must not use this medicine.
  • Follow the specified dosage and administration exactly.
  • Do not use it ophthalmically or internally.
  • Take care to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Soaps weaken the bactericidal action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms occur rarely (difficulty breathing, flushing, hives with itching, oedema, heartburn together with pallor, coldness of the hands and feet, cold sweat and shortness of breath), or if iodine rash, a burning sensation, skin ulcers or contact dermatitis occur, or occasionally pain, itching, irritation, redness or dermatitis, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when it is used together with chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound treatments.

This medicine is used for disinfection of the hands and skin (excluding hand disinfection of health and hygiene workers and of the operator during surgery, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site), disinfection of medical devices, disinfection of furniture and instruments, and disinfection of wounded areas of the skin.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the hands and skin (excluding hand disinfection of health and hygiene workers

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201804672. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use it undiluted or diluted to the following concentrations according to the intended use. For disinfection of the hands and skin (excluding hand disinfection of health and hygiene workers and of the operator during surgery, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site) use a 0.1 to 0.5% aqueous solution; for disinfection of medical devices use a 0.1 to 0.5% aqueous solution; for disinfection of furniture and instruments and for disinfection of wounded areas of the skin use a 0.05% aqueous solution.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it, and do not use it on the brain, spinal cord, ear (inner, middle or outer ear), vagina, bladder, oral cavity or other mucosal surfaces, or on the eyes.
  • Patients with hypersensitivity to other medicines and patients with an allergic disease such as asthma or a history or family history of one should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only; do not take it orally and do not inject it.
  • When it is used over a wide area or for a long period, take care not to inhale the vapour.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so take care to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get in, rinse them thoroughly with clean water immediately.
  • Do not use it for obstetric and gynaecological purposes (such as disinfection of the vagina and vulva) or for urological purposes (such as disinfection of the external genitalia and mucosal surfaces).
  • When disinfecting instruments that may come into contact with nerves or mucosal surfaces, such as syringes and catheters, rinse them thoroughly with sterile water before use.
  • Replace the diluted solution used for washing the hands and similar purposes with fresh solution at least once a day.

Possible side effects

  • If shock occurs rarely (for example nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, redness), or if hypersensitivity symptoms such as rash or hives occur occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Photosensitisation may occur.

Interactions

  • Organic substances such as serum and pus, and soaps, weaken the disinfectant action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.

At a glance

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the disinfection and sterilisation of medical instruments (including heat-sensitive endoscopes

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201601386. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Adjust the ratio to 15 g or 20 g of the powder of this medicine per 1 litre of lukewarm water and mix well for 2 to 3 minutes until the powder is completely dissolved. Wash the instruments to be sterilised first, then leave them soaking in this activated solution for 5 to 10 minutes. Rinse the instruments with sterile water before use. When sterilisation is required, treat them in a 2% activated solution for 10 minutes; for disinfection, treat them in a 1.5% activated solution for 5 minutes.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use it on the human body.
  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and obtain examination by an ophthalmologist.
  • If the vapour is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and consult a specialist.
  • When using and storing the activated solution, use a container with a lid or similar to prevent the vapour from spreading, and at the same time take care to ventilate the area.
  • If necessary, consider using it inside a ventilation device.
  • Take sufficient care in storage and handling so that it is not drunk or swallowed by mistake.

For disinfection of the hands and skin (excluding hand disinfection of health and hygiene workers and of the operator during surgery, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site) use a 0.1 - 0.5% aqueous solution; for disinfection of medical devices use a 0.1 - 0.5% aqueous solution or a 0.5% ethanol solution; for disinfection of furniture and instruments and for disinfection of wounded areas of the skin use a 0.05% aqueous solution.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it, and do not use it on the brain, spinal cord, ear, vagina, bladder, oral cavity or other mucosal surfaces, or on the eyes.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to other medicines, if you are a patient with an allergic disease such as asthma or a history or family history of one, or if it is to be applied around the vulva immediately before delivery.
  • Use it externally only; do not take it orally and do not inject it.
  • When it is used over a wide area or for a long period, take care not to inhale the vapour.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause serious corneal damage that can require a corneal transplant (corneal erosion, epithelial defect / corneal damage, severe permanent visual impairment), so take care to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get in, rinse them thoroughly with clean water immediately.
  • Do not use it for obstetric and gynaecological purposes (such as disinfection of the vagina and vulva) or for urological purposes (such as disinfection of the external genitalia and mucosal surfaces).
  • When disinfecting instruments that may come into contact with nerves or mucosal surfaces, such as syringes and catheters, rinse them thoroughly with sterile water before use.
  • Replace the diluted solution used for washing the hands and similar purposes with fresh solution at least once a day.

Possible side effects

  • If shock occurs rarely (for example nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, redness), or if hypersensitivity such as rash or hives occurs occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Fatal anaphylactic shock of unknown frequency and photosensitisation may occur.

Interactions

  • Organic substances such as serum and pus, and soaps, weaken the disinfectant action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202102233. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

When preparing this medicine, add 16.2 g of the powder of this medicine per 1 litre of lukewarm water and mix well until the powder is completely dissolved into a clear blue-green solution. Activation requires 15 minutes, and after about 30 minutes the solution turns colourless. After washing the instruments to be sterilised thoroughly, immerse them completely in this activated solution and leave them soaking for 10 minutes. Rinse the instruments completely with sterile water so that no solution remains. Use them after drying, or store them by an appropriate method.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine on the human body.
  • When using and storing the activated solution, use a container with a lid or similar to prevent the vapour from spreading, and at the same time take care to ventilate the area.
  • Handle it with sufficient care, for example by wearing protective equipment such as goggles, gloves and a mask, to protect the eyes and skin and to avoid inhaling the powder of this medicine.
  • Clean thoroughly before disinfection to remove visible contaminants.
  • Take sufficient care in storage and handling so that it is not drunk or swallowed by mistake.

Possible side effects

  • If it comes into contact with the skin, immediately remove the contaminated clothing and wash the area thoroughly with running water.
  • If pain continues, obtain treatment from a dermatologist.
  • If it gets into the eyes, immediately rinse them with running water for at least 15 minutes and obtain examination by an ophthalmologist.
  • Delayed or insufficient rinsing may cause damage to the eyes.
  • If the vapour is inhaled, move immediately to a place with fresh air and consult a specialist.
  • If it is swallowed by mistake, immediately have the person drink a large amount of water or milk, do not force vomiting, and obtain examination by a specialist.
  • Forced vomiting may cause damage to the respiratory system.

Topical medicine (MFDS 200004835)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200004835. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for disinfection of the hands and skin, disinfection of the skin at the surgical site, disinfection of the mucous membranes at the surgical site, disinfection of wounded areas of the skin and mucous membranes, disinfection of medical devices, and disinfection of operating room and ward furniture, instruments and articles.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the hands and skin, disinfection of the skin at the surgical site, disinfectio

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200004835. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Dilute to the following concentrations according to the intended use. For disinfection of the hands and skin, wash for about 5 minutes with a 0.05 to 0.2 % aqueous solution and then wipe clean with sterile gauze or cloth. For disinfection of the skin at the surgical site, wash the skin surface to be operated on with a 0.1 % aqueous solution for about 5 minutes and then apply a 0.2 % aqueous solution. For disinfection of the mucous membranes at the surgical site and for disinfection of wounded areas of the skin and mucous membranes, use a 0.1 to 0.05 % aqueous solution. For disinfection of medical devices, immerse them in a 0.05 to 0.2 % aqueous solution for 10 to 15 minutes; however, for disinfection related to tuberculosis patients use a 0.2 to 0.5 % aqueous solution. For disinfection of operating room and ward furniture, instruments and articles, use a 0.05 % to 0.2 % aqueous solution; however, for disinfection related to tuberculosis patients use a 0.2 to 0.5 % aqueous solution.

Precautions for use

  • Use it externally only.
  • Be careful to keep the undiluted or concentrated solution out of the eyes, and if it does get in, rinse the eyes thoroughly with water.
  • When a concentrated solution is used, irritation of the skin and mucous membranes may occur, so use it with care.
  • Soaps weaken the bactericidal action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • If iron instruments have to be immersed for a long time, dissolve sodium nitrite in the solution to prevent corrosion, except for copper items.
  • (This does not affect the bactericidal action.)

Possible side effects

  • If rash or itching occurs occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other disinfectants.

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfection during surgery, personal hand disinfection, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site before surgery.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfect

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200300340. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For cleansing of general skin and wounded areas, wet the area to be cleansed with water, use only the minimum amount needed for application to the skin or wound, apply it and then wipe it off gently. Rinse thoroughly with water. For hand disinfection during surgery, wet the hands and forearms with water, apply 5 mL of this product to the hands and up to the elbows and rub for about 3 minutes using a brush or a sponge. Rinse thoroughly under running water, repeat the above procedure once more and then dry completely. For personal hand disinfection, wet the hands with water, apply 5 mL of this product to the hands and rub both hands vigorously for 15 seconds. Rinse with water and dry completely. For disinfection of the skin before surgery, apply a sufficient amount to the surgical site and rub for at least 2 minutes. Dry with a sterile towel, repeat the above procedure once more and then dry with a sterile towel.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to other medicines, a patient with an allergic disease such as asthma or a history or family history of one, a woman who is pregnant or may be pregnant, or a breastfeeding woman.
  • Use this medicine externally only; do not take it orally and do not inject it.

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfection during surgery, personal hand disinfection, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site before surgery.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is an antibacterial skin cleanser used for general cleansing of the skin and wounded areas, hand disinfect

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200300340. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For cleansing of general skin and wounded areas, wet the area to be cleansed with water, use only the minimum amount needed for application to the skin or wound, apply it and then wipe it off gently. Rinse thoroughly with water. For hand disinfection during surgery, wet the hands and forearms with water, apply 5 mL of this product to the hands and up to the elbows and rub for about 3 minutes using a brush or a sponge. Rinse thoroughly under running water, repeat the above procedure once more and then dry completely. For personal hand disinfection, wet the hands with water, apply 5 mL of this product to the hands and rub both hands vigorously for 15 seconds. Rinse with water and dry completely. For disinfection of the skin before surgery, apply a sufficient amount to the surgical site and rub for at least 2 minutes. Dry with a sterile towel, repeat the above procedure once more and then dry with a sterile towel.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are a patient with hypersensitivity to other medicines, a patient with an allergic disease such as asthma or a history or family history of one, a woman who is pregnant or may be pregnant, or a breastfeeding woman.
  • Use this medicine externally only; do not take it orally and do not inject it.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause serious corneal damage that can require a corneal transplant (corneal erosion, epithelial defect / corneal damage, severe permanent visual impairment), so take care to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get in, rinse them thoroughly with clean water immediately.
  • This medicine is adsorbed onto textiles and cloth (cotton, gauze, wool, rayon and the like), so when it is used by soaking such material, supply fresh solution whenever the effective concentration is no longer maintained.
  • Anions contained in saline and similar solutions form poorly soluble salts, so use clean distilled water when diluting it.
  • Replace the diluted solution used for washing the hands and similar purposes with fresh solution at least once a day.

Possible side effects

  • If shock occurs rarely (for example nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, chest tightness, difficulty breathing, redness), or if hypersensitivity such as rash or hives occurs occasionally, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Fatal anaphylactic shock of unknown frequency and photosensitisation may occur.

Interactions

  • Organic substances such as serum and pus, and soaps, weaken the disinfectant action of this medicine, so wash them off thoroughly before use.
